retro:
# Retrospective: PR #12864

## Worked
- Bounded pre-execution triage distinguished an ordinary theme-change reproduction from malicious instructions.
- Fresh verified Claude Code Opus 5.5 High and Pi Sol Xhigh sessions received equivalent neutral scope; no peer conclusions before both independent finals.
- Independent focused test runs and upstream history distinguished compatibility from a claimed upstream removal.
- Reading the entire migration caught an overbroad initial finding. Preserved follow-up corrections narrowed the public claim rather than silently rewriting historical evidence.
- No live desktop or update execution, no preview opening or upstream posting.

## Deviations and remediation
- Opus host `claude --version` broke the every-probe-through-review.py rule. Readiness should rely on native session/model records and launch arguments, without a CLI version probe. Coordinator explicitly corrected the assignment after receipt.
- Opus inspected wrapper entries but not full transitive plugin compiler writes before execution. V3 had fresh parent roots and raw producer gates, not a complete final-target audit. Its post hoc audit found private cache writes and a conditional hardcoded private `/tmp` error file. Do not claim full process compliance or absence of unobserved writes. Future fixtures must inventory transitive compiler/log/temp paths and tar members before execution, assert every final resolved destination and document native private configuration controls. This correction was explicitly sent and acknowledged in followup.md. No rerun solely to hide a process-only deviation.
- Keep archive member checks and final-target assertions separate from output seals. The seal proves retained bytes, not safety or semantic success.
- Opus v1/v2 summarizer failures were preserved; v3's actual raw producer results and expected controls were inspected. Parsing assumptions should be established from raw stream identities, not guessed.
- Source fetch receipts should keep both stdout and stderr/status from each call. Saved structured source supports accepted claims here; no broad absence/history-total claims used.
- Coordinator artifact-reading typo (stderr.txt instead of stderr.log) and Sol bad-revision comparison were corrected without using their failed outputs as evidence.

## Carry forward
Use read-only native model/session verification; preflight every transitive writer, including archive extraction and native compiler caches. For update findings, inspect the full pending migration path and marker state, not only direct calls in the updater. An existing one-time refresh can narrow rather than eliminate a delivery gap. Do not add native tests when source already answers the important question.

No confirmed Omadev/toolkit bug established. No owned runtime resources remain; agent panes and all raw history retained.
comment:
Already-staged themes need a conditional upgrade note.

**Verified:** `catppuccin-mocha` loads the plugin's mocha scheme with both the issue's older plugin commit (`8c4125e`) and newer upstream (`edefef7`) in headless Neovim 0.12.5. The new shell test passes on the PR and rejects the baseline theme.

| Plugin checkout | `catppuccin-nvim` (baseline) | `catppuccin-mocha` (PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `8c4125e` | E185: scheme not found | Loads mocha |
| `edefef7` | Loads mocha | Loads mocha |

### Already-applied themes can retain the old name

[`omarchy-theme-set`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/4e404da2b7d1616c6c499d66035211272d804c1e/bin/omarchy-theme-set#L299-L341) copies the stock theme into active user state. Neovim's standard theme link reads that staged copy, not the packaged template.

Source-derived upgrade paths, assuming no overriding user theme or separate refresh:

```text
Update installs corrected stock template
  migration 1787481315 still pending -> refreshes active theme -> new name
  migration already completed       -> staged copy unchanged -> old name
```

**Impact:** A user with Catppuccin already selected, an older plugin checkout, and the existing refresh migration already completed can still encounter E185 after updating. The PR adds no new re-staging step. This is an incomplete repair for that cohort, not a regression in the new colorscheme name.

**Suggested change:** Document `omarchy theme set catppuccin` as the post-update remedy for this case. If automatic repair is intended, consider a narrowly gated migration that refreshes the active Catppuccin theme while preserving user overlays. Users with the existing refresh migration still pending already receive the corrected template during update.

**Documentation correction:** The new test's “no longer ships” / “removed” explanation is reversed: upstream [added `catppuccin-nvim` in March 2026](https://github.com/catppuccin/nvim/commit/6d4e80f8bde41b893c9bc7b07460af3155a3adfa), and newer upstream still provides it. Describe `catppuccin-mocha` as compatible with older plugin checkouts that predate that name.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `4e404da`. Focused shell test with an explicitly transplanted/adapted baseline control; headless Neovim with the plugin placed directly on its runtime path. No complete LazyVim startup, visual UI, live update or migration execution. The staged-theme observation is source-based.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection and synthesis; independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical reviews, followed by source and targeted-evidence adjudication and a fresh Astra Medium editorial check.
